preamble: Sixteen solutions contain related groups, three reversed, which are ignored in the cryptic part of their clues

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Regular fall-out in Pacific state

parts.note: the themed alphabet run, ignored by the cryptic reading

indicators.note: regular means taking every other letter of the word fall-out, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Radioactive fallout keeps landing on a small Pacific island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The run TUV is one of the preamble's alphabet sequences and gets no clue words. 'Regular' takes the alternate letters A, L, U of 'fall-out'; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuvalu is a small island country in the Polynesian region of the Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Age won't ruin garment

indicators.note: to ruin is to wreck, so the letters of the phrase are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: Getting older will not spoil your clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruin' rearranges the letters of 'Age won't'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea gown was a loose dress worn by women for afternoon tea at home.

clue.text: Word pictures of home turned over, given out first

indicators.note: first puts the rearranged word ahead of the other piece
out signals the word given is rearranged
turned over means the word for an animal's home is read backwards

parts.note: a sett is the burrow home of a badger

explanation.surface: Written sketches of a house are flipped and handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns GIVEN into VIGNE, put 'first'; 'turned over' makes TTES of SETT. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Vignettes are short descriptive passages, little sketches in words.

clue.text: To work with leading industrialist in US city is encouraging initially

indicators.note: in places the leading letter inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: leading takes the first letter of the word industrialist

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word encouraging

explanation.surface: A top industrialist working in an American city is a good sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading industrialist' looks like a tycoon working in the city, but it gives only an initial; 'is' is taken as it stands rather than as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to cooperate and keep in contact, to work with someone.

clue.text: Sport at the Mint!

definitions.meaning: a game played on horseback with mallets
a brand of ring-shaped British peppermint sweet

explanation.walkthrough: Polo mints are ring-shaped peppermints sold in Britain; 'at the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the equestrian ball game and the well-known brand of mint sweet.

clue.text: Little grebe departs with country bumpkin

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
the themed alphabet run, given no clue words
a hick is an unsophisticated rustic

explanation.surface: A small water bird leaves with a rural yokel.
explanation.walkthrough: D and HICK frame the themed run ABC; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The dabchick is the common name of the little grebe, a small diving water bird.

clue.text: Natural aptitude flash, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that a word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a flare is a sudden flash of light

explanation.surface: A gift for something shows itself in a quick burst, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: FLARE, a flash, sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural talent or knack for doing something well.

clue.text: The French king dismisses duke on WI island group

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: dismisses means the duke abbreviation is sent out of the king's name

parts.note: Edward is the name of several English kings

explanation.surface: A French monarch sacks a duke stationed on a West Indian island chain.
explanation.walkthrough: LE plus EDWARD without D gives EWARD; 'on' is a link. WI is West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leeward Islands are a chain in the West Indies, in the northern Lesser Antilles.

clue.text: Hound's two articles

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
the themed alphabet run, given no clue words
AN is the other form of the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dog is the subject of a couple of newspaper pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The two articles are A and AN, with the themed run FGH between them; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Afghan is a breed of long-haired hunting hound from Afghanistan.

clue.text: It's cut into thick slices to quench one's thirst

parts.note: to slake a thirst is to quench it; its first two letters come before the themed run
the themed alphabet run, given no clue words
the rest of the same word for quench, after the themed run

explanation.surface: Something sliced thickly is offered as a way of satisfying thirst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to quench one's thirst' reads as part of the definition's picture, but it is the wordplay; 'It's cut into thick slices' is the definition. The preamble's run sits inside the quenching word with no clue word for that step.
explanation.definitionFit: A slab cake is a large flat cake baked in a tray and sold cut into thick slices.

clue.text: Commander in chief holding a description of a vase

indicators.note: holding means the abbreviation for the commander contains the article

parts.note: C-in-C, written CIC, abbreviates commander in chief
the themed alphabet run, placed inside without clue words

explanation.surface: The commander in chief keeps an account of an urn.
explanation.walkthrough: C-in-C is the usual short form of commander in chief. The preamble's alphabet run, which the clue ignores, sits beside the A with no clue word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Canopic describes the jars in which ancient Egyptians stored the organs of the dead.

clue.text: Remain too long around mid- Devon. Indeed!

indicators.note: around means the letters picked from the county are turned back to front
mid- takes the middle letters of the word Devon, dropping its ends

parts.note: the themed alphabet run, given no clue words
aye, spelt AY, is an old word of agreement like indeed

explanation.surface: Someone lingers too long in the heart of Devon, and agrees they have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid- Devon' is the middle three letters of the county name, and 'around' turns them back; the preamble's run RST, ignored by the clue, follows. 'Indeed!' is aye, the old yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstay is to remain somewhere beyond the time allowed or welcome.

clue.text: Guide's turn of phrase

indicators.note: a turn of the word phrase means its letters are turned into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A guide has a particular way of putting things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn of phrase' looks like an idiom, but 'turn of' is the anagram signal working on 'phrase'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sherpa is one of the Himalayan people famous as mountain guides and porters.

parts.note: the themed alphabet run STU, entered backwards, with no clue words
the themed alphabet run STU, entered backwards, with no clue words

explanation.walkthrough: Only N comes from the clue; UTS is one of the themed runs written in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is informal for mad or wildly eccentric.

clue.text: Banker's unusually short kid

indicators.note: unusually signals the word short appears in an unusual letter order

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A banker has a remarkably small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges SHORT to ROTHS, followed by CHILD. The 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rothschild is the name of a famous European banking family, so it stands for a banker.

clue.text: Left thus, neglected and frozen

definitions.meaning: ignored and excluded, as one left out in the chill
exposed to the low temperature outdoors

explanation.walkthrough: One phrase: figuratively ignored, and literally out where it is cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means ignored or excluded, and taken literally means out where it is freezing.

clue.text: Fair article and note not very long ago

parts.note: fair means just
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A fair piece of writing and a memo arrived only recently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very long ago' is the definition at the end; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a moment ago, at that very time.

clue.text: Most of the historical account is deplorable

indicators.note: most of means the record word loses its final letters

parts.note: a chronicle is a historical account

explanation.surface: The bulk of the history is regrettable.
explanation.walkthrough: CHRONICLE without its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronic is informal British use meaning very bad or deplorable.

clue.text: Some notice about hearing

indicators.note: some of the word notice means a run of its letters is taken from inside it

explanation.surface: A bit of a notice concerns a legal hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside n-OTIC-e; 'about hearing' is the definition, not a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the medical adjective relating to the ear, so it concerns hearing.

clue.text: Mythical creature, so involved to become courtesan

indicators.note: involved means the answer and the word so are tangled together to make up the letters of courtesan

explanation.surface: A legendary beast gets mixed up in turning into a mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix the answer with SO and you get the letters of COURTESAN; 'to become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A centaur is a creature from Greek myth with a man's torso on a horse's body.

parts.note: RE is Latin-derived for about or concerning
the themed alphabet run STU, entered backwards, given no clue words

explanation.walkthrough: RE and B come from the clue; UTS is a themed run in reverse.

clue.text: Fab fish

definitions.meaning: an informal word for excellent or great
a flatfish related to the turbot

explanation.definitionFit: Brill is British slang for brilliant and also the name of a European flatfish.

clue.text: Party leader having last bit of butter that's gone off

parts.note: the themed alphabet run, given no clue words

indicators.note: the last bit of the word butter is its final letter
gone off suggests spoiling, which signals the letters of gone being rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Nicola Sturgeon led the Scottish National Party, so she is a party leader.

clue.text: Workers like penning books

NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.walkthrough: AS pens NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker ants are the sterile females that do a colony's labour.
